About the Position

The University of East Anglia (UEA) invites applications for a PhD position titled Design Optimisation of Brushless Doubly Fed Machines. The project is based in Norwich, United Kingdom, and focuses on improving the performance of brushless doubly fed machines (BDFMs) for offshore wind turbine generators.

Research Focus

The project addresses key research challenges in electrical engineering and renewable energy:

  • Low power density in BDFMs
  • Low power factor
  • Vibration in machine operation
  • Complex magnetic field behaviour

The aim is to improve BDFM performance and help position these machines as a competitive alternative to direct-drive and medium-speed permanent magnet generators for offshore wind applications.

Application dates

MilestoneDate
Application deadline30 November 2026

Application Process

  1. Submit a cover letter outlining your motivation and relevant experience.
  2. Include a CV.
  3. Provide academic transcripts.
  4. Supply contact information for two references.
  5. Contact the primary supervisor for details of the bench fee.
  6. Apply via the online portal.

About UEA

The University of East Anglia is a public research university in Norwich, England, with a strong reputation in energy research and a long-standing partnership with the Norwich Research Park.

Official Link

  • Application deadline: 30 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 30 November 2026. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
